cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is up on Mount Sinai inside the cloud, and he stays there forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24:18). That's where the LORD speaks to him. First order of business: tell the Israelites to bring Him an offering.

cards.question: God wants an offering from the Israelites. Who is Moses supposed to receive it from?

answers.text: Anyone whose heart moves him to give
Each man who is twenty or older
The leaders of the twelve tribes

cards.text: Then God lists what they can bring: gold, silver and bronze, colored yarn, fine linen, goat hair, leather, acacia wood, olive oil, spices and gemstones. Gold made the list, GOAT HAIR made the list, and friend, I spent years in a junk drawer and never made ANY list.

cards.question: God tells Moses the Israelites are to make Him a sanctuary so that He may ___ among them.
God tells Moses to design the tabernacle and its furnishings however he thinks best.

cards.text: First up: an ark of acacia wood, overlaid with pure gold inside and out, with a gold molding around it. God tells Moses to fasten four gold rings to its four feet and make poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold.

cards.question: The gold-covered poles slide into the rings on the sides of the ark. What are they for?

cards.text: And once those poles go into the rings, they stay there. Then God tells Moses to place the Testimony inside the ark, the Testimony God will give him.
Next comes a mercy seat of pure gold, the same length and width as the ark. At its two ends go two cherubim, all hammered from one piece of gold.
Their wings spread upward over the mercy seat, and they face each other, looking toward it. Then the mercy seat goes on top of the ark, with the Testimony inside.

cards.question: God talks about the place above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim over the ark. What does He say will happen there?

answers.text: The tribes will gather for feasts

cards.text: Then God moves on to a table of acacia wood, covered in pure gold, with a rim, a gold molding and four gold rings at its legs.

cards.question: Like the ark, the table gets poles so it can be carried.
God also wants plates, dishes, pitchers and bowls for the table, all of pure gold. What are the pitchers and bowls used for?

cards.text: And God tells Moses to place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Him.

cards.question: God says the Bread of the Presence goes on the table only on feast days.

cards.text: Then comes a lampstand of pure, hammered gold, all one piece, from its base and shaft up to its cups, buds and petals. Six branches come out of its sides, three on each side, and the branches and the lampstand itself carry cups shaped like almond blossoms.

cards.question: God tells Moses to set seven lamps on the lampstand so they ___ the area in front of it.

cards.text: Even the wick trimmers and their trays are pure gold. The lampstand and all its tools take a talent of pure gold.

God wraps up with one more reminder: see to it that everything is made according to the pattern shown on the mountain. Me, I STILL eyeball my chocolate chips, but friend, these plans aren't done yet, so stick around.
